transport.persistent: one connection per admitted local TLS peer; startup readonly inspection/resume uses an explicitly separate admitted-main connection
transport.framing: strict UTF-8 JSON object followed by exactly one LF; reject duplicate fields, NaN, floats, bools-as-integers and nonminimal integer lexemes; no unframed second request
transport.authorization: socket UID/GID are necessary only; SO_PEERPIDFD + PID1 mapping + MainPID/InvocationID/unit policy/candidate/context/current shared admission are mandatory

constants.drain_timeout: none: never relinquish the writer lease while an admitted child/effect remains unknown

storage.journal: root-owned locked journal with fsynced pending records before effects and atomic fsynced publication; never app/helper-writable
storage.journal_full: refuse without eviction/reexecution/factory reset; resume and readonly inspect remain available

boot_gate.rfkill_restore: systemd-rfkill.service and systemd-rfkill.socket masked in the new profile; gate verifies both inactive/masked/noMainPID, so neither boot nor late ADD can restore WLAN behind the gate
boot_gate.effect: WLAN-only soft block + durable NM WirelessEnabled=false, observed before NM starts every boot; never rfkill ALL; no profile or Bluetooth deletion/block
boot_gate.runtime_receipt: /run/inkyos-wlan-gate/closed.json bound to current boot and candidate
boot_gate.failure: prevent NM startup and keep WLAN closed; no bootstrap/new initialization implied

authority_invariants: OS verifies initialization_intent and initialization_receipt_digest against the real consumed OS initialization receipt; no file absence or boolean authorizes factory.

Owner, claim and current credential epoch are delegated only to the pinned admitted main after PreparedFactoryIdentity/owners.status(owner_id,owner_token,request_id=claim_request_id). No owner_token, QR secret or Wi-Fi secret crosses into OS IPC.
OS derives boot_id/candidate/context/mainInvocationID itself; the public owner binding does not substitute these observations.

Revalidate the connection/session/current graph before admitting EACH clock/country/radio effect. RESET/disconnect/expire/drain closes the local socket and revokes further admission; already admitted effects remain owned and drained.

GET firmware only; no vendor SET. Country comes explicitly from the app. No FR default or flash-time country. Refuse if the pinned native policy cannot establish requested firmware/kernel/channel/mapping evidence.
Each challenge nonce is real OS randomness and created/checked with CLOCK_BOOTTIME; retry never extends its 30s TTL.

Effect order: observed boot WLAN gate; fsynced PENDING; clock_settime_ns(CLOCK_REALTIME) and policy readback; iw reg set country and readbacks; NM WLAN enable plus readbacks. No scan/profile/connection secrets in setter.

Initial certificate publication consumes only a validated same-boot/current-session apply receipt, never a historical status or a fabricated ClockResult. A durable already-generated certificate candidate may only be finalized data-only with its identical intent/bytes under explicit recovery.
Same operation_id and exact canonical request hash returns durable state; differing arguments conflict. A recovered PENDING is UNCERTAIN, never auto-reexecuted.

Explicit recovery requires new operation_id + supersedes_operation_id + fresh challenge + authenticated owner; drain old effects and positively close/observe WLAN before a new effect cycle. Preserve old tombstones/receipts.

setup.inspect and setup.status are readonly and require current admitted-main proof but no old phone session. not_started/absence authorizes no mutation. inspect rediscovers operation/completion after lost replies.
Publication initial fingerprint is historical audit, not a permanent DER pin. Legitimate future certificates with the same UUID/key/SPKI remain accepted; no renewal from an unverified reboot clock.

setup.resume uses durable completion and fresh boot graph/WLAN gate, not an active owner/phone/old session. It does not replay old UTC or claim a new clock proof. Reapply/read back country before reopening WLAN; reconnect only the root-approved persistent profile.

Failure after WLAN activation triggers owned close-only cleanup: NM WirelessEnabled=false + WLAN soft block with real readbacks; no profile deletion. If closure is unconfirmed, expose uncertainty and retain SH/drains; never report readiness.

status.live.https_origin is null until actual Avahi name/state and current interface evidence match the persisted root-owned firstboot hostname. Do not infer origin from socket.gethostname, Host, SAN or IP. URL is explicit https://inky-<persisted32hex>.local:8443.

setup.complete binds current setup operation_id separately from publication.initial_setup_operation_id/publication_operation_id. After reboot/recovery the IDs may differ: require same UUID/SPKI and the actual historical initial publication, and an explicitly drained/superseded old effect workflow; never recreate the normal certificate.

setup.complete obtains the exact committed transaction from the attested helper plus independent current NM active UUID/profile/interface/IPv4 checks, then root alone writes initial immutable completion and network-head revision1.

A normal owner-authorized Wi-Fi change may create a later committed helper transaction. On resume OS asks setup-only inspect_latest_committed, verifies no pending/uncertain journal state and the exact latest durable committed profile against NM, and atomically updates a separate root network-head. Initial profile/tx stay historical audit, not forever pins.

An absent/pending/uncertain helper journal keeps NORMAL_RECOVERY with WLAN closed, never a fallback to an arbitrary or original profile. It neither deletes root completion nor reopens factory. A subsequent explicit authenticated normal-profile recovery may make a new genuine committed transaction.

helper_inspect_committed.authorized_peer: only pinned setup-service root peer, confirmed via SO_PEERPIDFD + PID1 MainPID/InvocationID/candidate. Never forwarded from owner/media wire namespace.

error_meanings.not_found: No retained committed transaction (or exact id/owner absent). No profile may be inferred.
error_meanings.busy: A nonfinal/pending network transaction exists; no committed selection is authorized.
error_meanings.not_ready: Journal invalid/partial/uncertain, NM unavailable/inconsistent, or required live/persistent metadata unavailable.
error_meanings.permission_denied: Peer is not the admitted exact setup service.

helper_inspect_committed.boot_id_meaning: boot_id and nm_unique_owner are sampled for THIS observation from actual kernel/current NM bus owner. commit_boot_id/commit_nm_unique_owner derive only from the historical committed journal instance; never reuse them as current observations.
helper_inspect_committed.hash_meaning: observation_sha256 = SHA256(canonical JSON of exactly all returned NetworkObservation fields excluding observation_sha256; sorted keys, ASCII, compact separators, trailing LF). The OS recomputes it over this attested peer response. It is an observation binding, not a signature, HMAC, hash of secret intent.key, nor a journal-file authenticity claim.

idempotency_exclusions: current observer invocation/boot, retained separately in original receipt
initial_publication_attestation: Pinned admitted main validates the real PreparedFactoryIdentity initial publication journal and current same-UUID/key/SPKI identity; supplies public publication_operation_id, initial_setup_operation_id, historical initial_certificate_sha256. These initial IDs may differ from the latest setup effect operation_id after explicit drained/superseded recovery. OS imports no Studio code and reads no private key. Same immutable initial publication can survive legitimate leaf renewal and later setup operations.
resume_when_helper_or_network_missing: Completion remains root authority for NORMAL mode; original owner need not still be active. Query latest committed only via actually attested helper. If journal absent/pending/uncertain or profile absent/conflicting, keep NORMAL_RECOVERY and WLAN closed; do not fall back to the first/original profile and do not reopen QR/factory. Disconnected latest committed metadata can have ipv4=[]; independent native profile verification precedes country/radio/activation, and readiness requires fresh actual IP afterwards.

unit_policy.scope: separate new role; initialization IPC retains empty capabilities; no Studio import/execution in setter

helper_inspect_latest_committed.authorized_peer: same setup-only pidfd/InvocationID/candidate guard as inspect_committed; no owner/media/app forwarding
helper_inspect_latest_committed.selection: last phase=committed/state=committed record in existing retained journal update order; journal must be present/validated, no pending/uncertain active transaction; verify real NM persistent profile id/UUID/interface before returning
helper_inspect_latest_committed.network_down: ipv4 may be [] and active_profile_uuid null, never pretend network ready; profile metadata remains subject to independent OS NM recross-check
helper_inspect_latest_committed.failure: absent/pending/uncertain/invalid/ambiguous -> fixed unavailable/not_ready, NORMAL_RECOVERY with WLAN closed; no arbitrary or first-profile fallback

error_meanings.not_found: No retained committed transaction (or exact id/owner absent). No profile may be inferred.
error_meanings.busy: A nonfinal/pending network transaction exists; no committed selection is authorized.
error_meanings.not_ready: Journal invalid/partial/uncertain, NM unavailable/inconsistent, or required live/persistent metadata unavailable.
error_meanings.permission_denied: Peer is not the admitted exact setup service.

helper_inspect_latest_committed.boot_id_meaning: boot_id and nm_unique_owner are sampled for THIS observation from actual kernel/current NM bus owner. commit_boot_id/commit_nm_unique_owner derive only from the historical committed journal instance; never reuse them as current observations.
helper_inspect_latest_committed.hash_meaning: observation_sha256 = SHA256(canonical JSON of exactly all returned NetworkObservation fields excluding observation_sha256; sorted keys, ASCII, compact separators, trailing LF). The OS recomputes it over this attested peer response. It is an observation binding, not a signature, HMAC, hash of secret intent.key, nor a journal-file authenticity claim.

canonicalization.json: UTF-8/ASCII canonical sorted keys, separators comma/colon without spaces, one trailing LF
canonicalization.record_sha256: SHA256 canonical record excluding its own record_sha256 field; integrity binding, not a signature or authorization
canonicalization.request_sha256: SHA256 canonical object of exactly idempotency_material; workflow and owner fields from admitted setup.open, operation fields from setup.apply; excludes RPC id and transient observer/session fields
canonicalization.source_observation_sha256: NetworkHead stores the independently recomputed NetworkObservation.observation_sha256 exactly as defined in helper contract.

normal_data_only_continue: Backend wire system_setup.continue is an explicit current-owner/claim/session-authorized app mutation. It may use readonly setup.inspect/status as historical evidence only to finalize identical already-durable initial certificate intent/bytes; no new clock grant and no reexecution of OS apply. If no candidate bytes survive or identity/lineage conflict, fresh operation/challenge is required; no auto-recertification of an existing normal identity.
